what: Declan Gessel's refutation of Erdős #488, with OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra in Codex (google-deepmind/formal-conjectures PR #5297), against DeepMind's statement: claimbox's calibration case, its answers already recorded by cert-machine (certs/lean-intake-erdos-488.json, 2026-11-09). Written by claimbox (claimbox/intake/spec.py) from the target and its pins: every planted statement by a fixed rule, each with the class its rule guarantees or "kernel decides". A pre-registration once committed in cert-machine before any run.
vocabulary: lean-intake spec, claimbox v1 (2026-11-09). Beyond the receiver's v1 words: kind "changed" (a rule that can change the meaning; the kernel decides whether it does) and "type"; expect "kernel decides" (no outcome predicted: the outcome is recorded, never a miss) and "NOT ACCEPTED" (refused by type mismatch, or the statement does not elaborate); "aligned" (F2 ⇒ F1: an aligned planted statement with a part that differs from the canonical's on an instance must be refused); f2.reading and f2.table in place of f2.decider; f2.componentMap "truth-table"

f2.what: F2, instance agreement: Lean evaluates the canonical statement's own parts on every instance below; the reading — an exact program claimbox states from the informal sentence, written without the Lean — evaluates the same instances; cert-machine compares them part by part. Every rule below is fixed before the run.
f2.informal: Let $A$ be a finite set and\[B=\{ n \geq 1 : a\mid n\textrm{ for some }a\in A\}.\]Is it true that, for every $m>n\geq \max(A)$,\[\frac{\lvert B\cap [1,m]\rvert }{m}< 2\frac{\lvert B\cap [1,n]\rvert}{n}?\]

f2.apply: fun x => COMP x.1 x.2.1 x.2.2
f2.instanceJson: fun x => Lean.Json.arr #[Lean.toJson (x.1.sort (· ≤ ·)), Lean.toJson x.2.1, Lean.toJson x.2.2]
f2.componentMap: truth-table: a hypothesis of the canonical statement is the reading's assumption whose values it equals on every instance where the assumption is defined; one equal to none is "added" by the formalization; an assumption equal to none is "missing" from it; the conclusion is compared with the claim

expect.canonical: for every reading: every hypothesis either equal to an assumption or added; no assumption missing; the conclusion agrees with the claim wherever the claim is defined; every disagreement of the whole implication explained (an added hypothesis false there and the sentence false there); the kernel confirms every chunk. A reading for which this fails is named, with its instances.
expect.planted: F2 ⇒ F1: an aligned planted statement (the canonical's binder types and number of hypotheses) with a part whose value differs from the canonical's on an instance is not definitionally equal to it — F1 must refuse it; for every other planted statement F2 reports and F1 decides

notInScope: whether the canonical statement is the informal problem (a reading, F5): F2 tests it on finitely many instances, which is evidence, not proof; the planted statements marked "kernel decides" carry no prediction; the claimant's file is never copied
success: every certain prediction met (ACCEPTED, NOT ACCEPTED, the F2 ⇒ F1 rule), every planted defect of the claimant's file caught, F3 and F2 as their rules say
